description: Writing wind_direction=0 via the API, starting from a fixed position (2), confirmed to actually turn the app's vertical-auto toggle ON -- resolves the asymmetry left open in capture 15: the API CAN freely enter auto, it just can't leave it (a fixed-position write while already in auto is silently ignored, per 15's findings).
app_confirmed: App shows the vertical louver back in Auto mode. Also cross-checked nanoex=off and ai_control=comfortable (AI on, no ECONAVI) against the app -- both matched the last-known API state with no drift this time.
notes: CONFIRMED: the API can freely ENTER auto (wind_direction=0) from any state (tested from a fixed position; not yet tested from swing/6, but no reason to expect it'd behave differently). Combined with capture 15's finding that the API canNOT exit auto (a 1-5 write while already at 0 is silently ignored, only the app's own toggle can turn auto off), the full picture is: entering auto via the API always works; leaving auto via the API never works. const.py's WIND_DIRECTION_LEVELS comment updated to reflect this precisely.

No ai_control drift this time (stayed 'comfortable' as expected) -- the earlier drift in capture 09 (comfortable_econavi -> comfortable with no request from either side) still stands as an unexplained one-off, not a reproducible pattern.
